data.one_liner: An interpreter and runtime for executing Dart code dynamically.
data.what_it_does: d4rt is a Dart-written interpreter and runtime that allows you to execute Dart code dynamically in your applications. It includes AST caching, execution limits, code introspection, and a security sandboxing system.
use_when: You need to execute user-provided or dynamically loaded Dart code at runtime.
You want to build scripting or plugin systems within your Dart/Flutter application.
You require execution limits and sandboxing to restrict dangerous operations like filesystem or network access.
avoid_when: You are looking for standard ahead-of-time (AOT) or just-in-time (JIT) compilation for performance-critical production code.
You do not need dynamic script interpretation or runtime code evaluation.
strengths: Full generics support and runtime type validation
Security sandboxing with permission-based module restrictions
Precompiled scripts and AST caching for better performance
weaknesses: Interpreted code execution is inherently slower than native compiled code
Certain advanced native interactions require specific permission grants
data.setup_notes: Add d4rt to pubspec.yaml and configure security permissions via code if executing restricted operations.
